Highlight2.name: Odd Fellow Says Hello
Highlight2.info: Put your wits to the test with Odd Fellow Says Hello, a game of wordplay and fun! In each round, you’ll face four words—but one doesn’t belong. Is it a trick of meaning or a subtle twist of context? Gather your friends or challenge yourself to find the Odd Fellow before time runs out. Perfect for quick thinkers, word lovers, and anyone who loves a clever challenge. Are you sharp enough to spot the odd fellow? Odd fellow says hello!

Highlight3.name: When The Flower Stops Breathing
Highlight3.info: When The Flower Stops Breathing is an interactive kinetic sculpture composed of a cluster of mechanical flowers that continuously bloom and close, echoing the subtle rhythms of living ecosystems. It asks a simple but uneasy question: what happens to a system when it is constantly observed, approached, and disturbed?
Highlight3.summary: Kinetic sculpture that reacts to crowds
Highlight3.role: Design · code · fabrication · Python, OpenCV, Raspberry Pi
Highlight3.preview: Sixteen servo-driven flowers bloom calmly at a respectful distance and start to stutter when people crowd in. OpenCV tracks the viewers. My senior thesis.

Highlight5.name: Mirror Selfie
Highlight5.info: Through this project, I explored the interaction between people and mirrors. When walking by mirrors, I noticed that people tend to subconsciously stare at the mirrors back to themselves to check their own appearance or to take mirror pictures. However, after I learnt about spy two-way mirrors, I felt more cautious interacting with mirrors due to my paranoia of being spied on. For this project titled “Mirror-Selfie”, I am embodying my fear of being stared back at by the mirror or anything behind the mirror. Using a camera with the OpenCV Python library, I detect faces and print out a frame of the moment when anyone looks into the mirror.
Highlight5.preview: A two-way mirror installation. Face detection prints a frame the moment someone checks their reflection.

Highlight7.name: Dot Map
Highlight7.info: Dot Map is a long-form generative art that uses a Javascript algorithm to create a 25 x 25 matrix that puts colors in random circles within the squares. This art explores how pseudo-randomness, structure, and computation collaborate to create uniqueness. Using the modulo operator, each circle is assigned with a random number. The system decides which circles in the grid becomes colored, and which ones stays white. This rule creates a pattern that feels random while still following a consistent logic. Beyond its visual output, Dot Map also creates a sense of time. Viewers wait as the colors reveals itself square by square, watching the system produce the art instead of receiving a finished result. Once the pattern fully appears, the piece continues to function as an interactive environment rather than a static image. Users can still engage with the system by hovering their mouse over each grid to enlarge the circles. Dot Map does not end when the randomness stops, it remains alive, inviting interaction that can only happen through the blockchain medium.
Highlight7.preview: A JavaScript algorithm fills a 25 × 25 grid with randomized color circles, so every output is a new piece.

Rock Paper Scissor.name: Rock Paper Scissor
Rock Paper Scissor.info: Rock-Paper-Scissors generator that displays a random symbol (rock, paper, or scissors) upon each mouse click, featuring pixelated visual language and retro-inspired design.
Rock Paper Scissor.summary: Pixel-art rock-paper-scissors: one click, one throw

Data Portrait.name: Data Portrait
Data Portrait.info: For this project, I spent a week tracking my personal habit to create a data-self portrait. This sketch is divided into 7 different parts (shown by the guidelines in the background); the first section determines the first day which was Wednesday. The section goes up until the last day, which is Tuesday and the days change based on the mouse location. The density and the size of the orange form is the amount of time that I spent talking to people on the phone (in minutes), while the density and size or the purple form is based on the total minutes I spent interacting with people in real life. Lastly, the row of squares that travels from left to right shows the amount of people I interacted with per day.
Data Portrait.summary: A week of my social habits, drawn as a self-portrait

Time Keeper.name: Time Keeper
Time Keeper.info:
Conventional clocks mark seconds, minutes, and hours according to a 24 hour cycle. This segmented, discrete, and regimented approach to parsing time is not universal in terms of capturing and measuring of experience.
Time often feels fluid and variable, moving swiftly at moments and slowing to a near standstill at others. This time-keeper clock experimentation seeks to visualize these fluctuations in the perceived speed of time. This project explores the potential of design as a tool for psychological time modulation, offering a unique perspective on the relationship between time perception and mental states.

Dial when mouse is on the left side of the screen:
Slower paced
Dial when mouse is on the right side of the screen:
Faster paced
Time Keeper.summary: A clock that speeds up and slows down the way time feels

Sunrise.name: Sunrise
Sunrise.info:
The rapid development of technology is slowly affecting how people go about their daily task. It has been deeply incorporated in the everyday life seamlessly like it is natural. Since nature and technology are two contradicting topics I wondered what is the true relationship between nature and technology? Is it true that technologies can take over natural resources and to what extent? How can technology be useful as a substitution of natural resources? and what about nature is irreplaceable?
I attempted to build an artificial sun replacement with leds and a motor running it. The idea is to have the led illuminate brighter as the space gets darker, vice-versa.
As some people have trouble managing time between the night and day time, I expected this project to bridge that transition, bringing the sunlight indoors when it is gone from the outdoors.
Sunrise.summary: An LED 'artificial sun' that brightens as the room gets dark

Hue Hunter.summary: Find the red square by following colour and pitch

Time Machine.name: Time Machine
Time Machine.info:
Time is a universal yet profoundly subjective experience, perceived differently depending on individual circumstances and contexts. Although every person has the same 24 hours in a day, the passage of time can feel faster or slower based on activities, environments, and interpersonal interactions. This variability highlights the surreal and fluid nature of time.
In philosophy, time is often regarded as a metaphysical concept, defying material definition. The progression of moments—the future becoming the present and the present transitioning into the past—creates a dynamic interplay that can distort our perception of time. In group settings, for example, the flow of conversation and actions can seemingly compress time, reducing the perceived gaps between past, present, and future.
This reflection underscores the intangible and abstract nature of time. It extends beyond the numerical representation of hours on a clock, often relying on intuition and perception. This abstraction challenges traditional notions of time, emphasizing its fluid and subjective essence.
Time Machine.summary: Acrylic and electronics piece about how time feels in a group

Pinterest Case Study.name: Pinterest Case Study
Pinterest Case Study.info:
A UX teardown of Pinterest: what makes it work, where it breaks, and how I would fix it.

Value proposition. Pinterest is a discovery and search engine for visual inspiration. It connects people to a broader audience and lets them save, group, and organize ideas.

Why it beats its competitors. The feed is curated to each user’s interests rather than what’s popular. Its masonry grid never breaks abruptly, so people keep scrolling and discovering, unlike Instagram or TikTok. Motion cues and animations keep it playful rather than overwhelming. It has one clear purpose, displaying images to organize into boards, which makes it easy for people of all ages to understand. And it isn’t about followers or likes, but personal discovery, collaboration, and visual brainstorming, which makes it a stress-free social media environment.

I found three pain points, each with a proposed fix below.

doc3.caption: Shown in relation to the content, with a similar size and format

doc4.caption: A subscription option to remove them completely

doc5.caption: A temperature scale on every page to change how relevant the content is

doc6.caption: The menu at the top right

doc7.caption: Advanced settings to adjust several parameters

doc8.caption: A movable temperature button that doesn’t clutter the interface

doc10.caption: Sticky notes for leaving comments on a board

doc12.caption: A new “Annotate” tool for writing anywhere on the screen

doc13.caption: A new “Sort Mode” for swiping through pins left and right

Pinterest Case Study.summary: Why the feed feels calm, and where it breaks

Current Pinterest.text: The web and app as they are today: a masonry feed of images to save into boards.

Fix 1 · Ads.text: Problem: random video ads break the flow of exploring. Fix: keep ads image-based, less frequent, and related to what you’re searching for, so they blend into the feed, plus a subscription option to remove them completely.

Fix 2 · Discovery.text: Problem: once Pinterest learns what you like, similar content keeps showing up, creating a bubble that restricts discovery. Fix: a “temperature” control to choose how random or specific the feed is.

Fix 3 · Collaboration.text: Problem: boards can be shared, but there are no notes or stickers to comment or vote, so collaborators go back and forth with another product. Fix: FigJam-style tools on boards.
